# Provider-inert agent fixture

Run `python3 packages/tests/fixtures/agent-inert-convex/run.py` only when loopback ports 3540/3541 are free. The runner preflights both ports, starts a fresh local backend, sets `E2E_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1` and an empty `BOAT_API_KEY` before sync, runs the backend flow, and stops its own process. It temporarily copies `agentFixture.ts` into this checkout's backend solely for the disposable deployment; never deploy that fixture to a shared backend. The flow independently verifies the exact port pair, empty Boat and R2 configuration, and the telemetry flag.

The real product enqueue logic is invoked through a fixture-only adapter that supplies configuration presence as a boolean; no Boat credential is supplied. The adapter replaces only scheduled `agent/actions/run:tick` jobs with a fixture no-op and rejects any other scheduled target. The abort handler uses the same adapter. A fixture-only no-op watchdog supplies the lease; the real finish handler cancels it. The test covers queued messages and attachment retention after abort, cross-owner app and attachment denial, competing claim, stop invalidation, history, token rotation, and CLI status using the real product handlers and agent component.

The registered production enqueue mutation still reads `BOAT_API_KEY` at the same point and fails closed when absent. This fixture does not exercise the public send action's provider configuration check, the real scheduled worker, Boat dispatch, or remote stop. The prior unsafe proof remains disabled as `agent-queued-proof.ts.txt` for reference.

The runner also executes `paid-test.py` against synthetic users and real Convex transactions. Its fixture adapter explicitly selects the paid admission path, supplies a local in-memory balance response to the real credit parser, and substitutes scheduled worker, uncertainty and stop functions with no-ops. The nonempty string passed to the parser is a fixture sentinel, not a provider credential; the injected request function never performs I/O. It checks insufficient balance, two competing app admissions sharing one user session, one competing debit claim, and an unknown result holding the session and rolling back further queued work. The production mutation retains its configured payments default. This does not exercise a real provider, continuous renewal, provider idempotency, or successful billing/fulfillment.

The paid fixture also injects a confirmed initial debit result for a separate synthetic user and checks real session transactions at `paidUntil - 1`, `paidUntil`, and `paidUntil + 1`. Another admission in that active window must pass a fresh mocked balance check and reuses the same session and debit. The fixture then moves that synthetic session's deadline into the past: access and new admission fail, and the real claim handler transitions the expired active session to stopping without another debit. Scheduled boundary, notice, and stop actions are replaced with no-ops. This is an exact state-boundary check, not a continuous-renewal or provider-settlement guarantee.

`paid-tick.test.mjs` runs in its own Bun subprocess from the product-only `agent-credits.test.ts`. It executes the actual worker tick and `computeAccess` with paid mode enabled only in the subprocess. Boat, debit, authorization and network calls use inert or fail-fast test adapters; simulated expiry and deletion during awaited operations check subsequent dispatch fencing. It does not exercise a Convex transaction, real credentials or provider behavior.

`paid-credential.test.mjs` runs in an isolated Bun subprocess with paid mode enabled and an in-memory database adapter. It invokes the real bootstrap, issue and authenticate handlers while Boat file and command operations are inert captures. It verifies active credential use, exact-deadline denial and hold/deletion/stopped/invalid-session-owner denial, without authenticating a real user or testing Convex transactions. It also verifies mismatched bootstrap owner and app inputs are rejected before issuance or any remote credential write.
